title: kv: improve cache eviction, fragmentation compaction and spillover/paging support
author: Miguel Santos
description: Motivation: KV cache memory fragmentation and unbounded growth of inactive cache shards has caused tail latency regressions and OOMs on constrained nodes. This PR introduces a multi-pronged approach: 1) a compacting allocator for KV shards that reduces fragmentation by coalescing free segments at runtime; 2) a spillover manager that transparently pages cold KV entries to host memory / tmpfs and optionally to persistent storage for private deployments; 3) soft and hard watermarks with eviction heuristics that combine LRU, segment age, and token-weighted cost; 4) integration with continuous batching and the request scheduler so hot keys are pinned and rarely-evicted, reducing cache churn; and 5) metrics and tracing hooks to observe paging, compaction, and eviction decisions. Implementation notes: Added runtime/kv/allocator.rs for the compacting allocator and fragmentation scanner; runtime/kv/spillover.rs implements spill-to-host pager and async restore path; runtime/kv/evict_policy.rs encodes the new multi-factor eviction scoring; runtime/scheduler/batcher.rs was extended to surface per-key hotness signals and to inform the cache manager about batch-affinity; a new feature flag kv.spillover.enabled controls paging in hosted vs private deployments. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is unchanged unless kv.spillover.enabled is set and watermarks are configured. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks show a 35% reduction in peak device memory for long-running chat workloads and a 7% improvement in p99 generation latency under memory pressure due to reduced GC/eviction churn. End-to-end canary on dedicated nodes initially failed due to an edge-case race in async restore; that was fixed in commit 4 and the canary passed. The description below summarizes commits, changed files, review threads, CI checks and merge notes.
commits: 1) Add compacting allocator and fragmentation scanner (runtime/kv/allocator.rs)
2) Implement spillover manager with async page-in/out and config knobs (runtime/kv/spillover.rs)
3) New eviction policy combining LRU, segment age and token-weight (runtime/kv/evict_policy.rs)
4) Scheduler integration: batcher exposes hot-key hints and pinning API (runtime/scheduler/batcher.rs)
5) Add tests and integration harness for paging/restore (integration_tests/kv_spillover_test.py)
6) Docs and observability: add metrics, tracers and docs (docs/kv-eviction.md, benchmarks/kv_memory/README.md)
7) Fix race in async restore path and increase timeouts in canary (follow-up commit)
8) Minor lint/test fixes and CI ergonomics
review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: Can you clarify the cost model used in the eviction score? Specifically how token-weight interacts with segment age. Reply: Miguel Santos: The score is a linear combination: score = alpha*LRU_score + beta*segment_age_norm + gamma*(token_count * token_cost). alpha/beta/gamma are tunable via kv.eviction.weights. We chose conservative defaults after grid search on ENG-987 workloads.

Daniel Park: The spillover path uses tmpfs by default; what are the failure modes on nodes without enough host RAM? Reply: Miguel Santos: There are two layers: soft/hard watermarks trigger spill and then compaction; if host memory is insufficient spill can be routed to configured persistent path (kv.spillover.persistent_path) and we expose a throttle and circuit-breaker which degrades to no-spill eviction once the circuit trips.

Ravi Patel: Observability looks comprehensive but we need a Grafana dashboard. Request: please add a dashboard JSON. Reply: Miguel Santos: Added metrics YAML and a dashboard stub in observability/dashboards/kv_spillover.json included in a follow-up commit.

Aisha Kapoor (requested changes): Handle race when async restore is cancelled by scheduler preemption. Reply: Miguel Santos: Fixed in commit 7 by introducing a restore token and safe-cancel path, added unit test.
Daniel Park: Approved after addressing race and adding unit tests.
Ravi Patel: Approved overall; small nits about doc wording addressed in follow-up.
ci_checks: perf-canary: initial run failed (race on async restore) -> fixed -> rerun passed
merge_info: Merged via squash on 2026-02-25. Commit message: 'kv: improve cache eviction and add spillover/paging support. Addresses ENG-987, ENG-1024.'
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adds compacting allocator to reduce fragmentation, introduces configurable spillover/paging of cold KV entries to host/persistent storage, implements a multi-factor eviction policy (LRU + segment age + token-weight), integrates hot-key pinning with the continuous batching scheduler, and adds metrics/tracing for eviction and paging events. Default behavior unchanged unless kv.spillover.enabled is enabled. Benefits: lower peak device memory and reduced p99 tail latency under memory pressure.
